SMTO-API-0012 — Too many attempts, so SMTO is pausing this for a moment

GUID: 226ba40d-8576-4baa-9b4e-8070ca54d503
Slug: api-rate-limited
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • SMTO is briefly refusing more requests of this kind because too many arrived in a short time, for example several sign-in or password attempts in a row.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait at least one minute before trying again. If the message gives a specific wait time, wait that long instead. SMTO pauses sign-in and password attempts for about a minute after five tries, and attempts during the pause won't get through.
  2. Don't click the button repeatedly while you wait. Each extra click is another request, which keeps SMTO at its limit.
  3. If you were signing in or changing your password, check your username and password carefully before your next attempt. Every try counts toward the limit, so one careful attempt is better than several quick ones.

What success looks like

  • Your next attempt, after the wait, is accepted.

If it still fails

  • If you were changing something, check whether it already happened before repeating it. If the pause keeps coming back, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An SMTO endpoint returned HTTP 429 (for example portal sign-in or password-change throttling with Retry-After: 60) and no more specific registered cause applied.

What this means

  • HTTP enrichment maps an otherwise unclassified status 429 to the rate-limit category. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • HTTP enrichment maps an otherwise unclassified status 429 to the rate-limit category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect any returned retry window and owning service policy; no fixed waiting time is implied when absent.

How to fix it

  • Honor the Retry-After header when present and back off instead of retrying in a loop. Portal sign-in and password-change limits allow five attempts per client per minute (50 across all clients) and two concurrent verifications; confirm whether any uncertain state-changing request already took effect before replaying it.
  • Respect the returned retry window when present and the service's documented rate policy; avoid an immediate retry loop.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A later permitted request respects the actual returned retry guidance.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
